facts.F16: How a local time reading is judged. The measure script alternates 5 pairs: the before side is an untracked copy of the before-commit test file next to the real one (deleted by the script on exit), the after side is the rewritten file. A pair is valid only if all four 1-minute load-average samples (start and end of both runs) are at or under half the cores and every test passed. Fewer than 3 valid pairs prints unmeasured, machine loaded, exits non-zero, and is never retried in a loop. The ratio is the median over valid pairs of after/before summed per-test seconds (assertionResults duration in ms from the JSON report; the script deletes the report first and refuses a stale one). The ratio, not the seconds, is judged, so machine speed cancels. CI judgement (median of at least 4 main runs of test-timings-frontend CSVs, as the baseline) happens after the push and is not a slice gate.
